newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delhaize sees profit, sales growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Delhaize sees profit, sales growth in '97.

text.p: Etablissements Delhaize Freres et Cie "Le Lion" SA said on Wednesday 1996 group net profit rose 15 percent and added it expected sales and profits to grow further in 1997.
The Belgian retailer also plans 14 billion Belgian francs ($402.6 million) of investments this year.

"In 1997 113 new sales outlets will be opened. This together with the takeover of the 100 Kash n' Karry supermarkets acquired at the end of 1996 by (U.S. unit) Food Lion enables the Delhaize "Le Lion" group to look forward to continued growth in sales and profits," it said in a statement on 1996 results.

In 1996 group net profit rose 15.6 percent to 4.354 billion francs and sales climbed 11.9 percent to 412.3 billion. At constant exchange rates the rises would have been 11.7 percent and eight percent respectively, Delhaize said.
"(The 15.6 percent rise) is an excellent growth figure," the group's managing director, Gui de Vaucleroy, told a news conference to present the results.
He said that in 1996 Delhaize "Le Lion" had slightly increased its market share of total food sales in Belgium to 13.2 percent from 13 percent.
"The food market (in Belgium) is stagnant. Consumer confidence was not there and is not present at the beginning of this year," De Vaucleroy said.
But he believed that with the opening of new stores in 1997 there would be growth in a "difficult market".
"1997 will be a difficult year in Europe, though in the Czech Republic (our) growth will be easier," he added. "But 1996 was not an easy year (either) so I'm very confident for this year."
"We have excellent marketing tools, good people and good logistics - we are well prepared for increasingly tough competition," he said.
De Vaucleroy repeated that the Delhaize group was studying expansion in Asia, though declined to say which country or countries it was looking at.

He added that a deal was expected by the end of the year and said Delhaize had the "necessary financial resources" available for such a venture. The group would also continue to grow in Europe and the United States.
At the end of 1996 the Delhaize group operated 1,700 sales outlets in five countries, after 124 stores were opened during the financial year. ($ = 34.77 Belgian Francs)
